name: Non-Specific Low Back Pain — AR Profile (Adaptive Responder)
description: Evidence-based 12-week program with standard progression for Adaptive Responders. Focus: Balanced training without specific behavioral modification.
pain_rule: Pain max. 4/10 during exercise. Follow the 24-hour rule.
evidence_base: Hayden et al. (2021): Exercise therapy - Cochrane Review
O'Sullivan et al. (2018): Cognitive Functional Therapy

phase_education.1:
**Phase 1: Building Foundations (Weeks 1–4)**

Your screening shows an adaptive pattern: you have a balanced relationship between activity and recovery. That's a good foundation.

**Goal of this phase:** Improve core stability and mobility.

**Your strategy:**
- Focus on core activation and controlled movement
- Pain max. 4/10 during exercise
- Regular training (3x/week) for consistent adaptation
- Focus on technique — clean execution is more important than volume

**Scientific basis:** NICE Guidelines (2020): A structured exercise program is the first-line intervention for non-specific LBP.
phase_education.2:
**Phase 2: Increasing Resilience (Weeks 5–8)**

You have a solid foundation. Now we build strength and capacity.

**Goal of this phase:** Progressive increase of strength and endurance.

**Your strategy:**
- Add weights when form is solid
- Progressive overload: small, consistent increases
- Pain max. 4/10 remains the limit
- Balance between loading and recovery

**Scientific basis:** Hayden et al. (2021): Moderate-to-high intensity exercise shows the best outcomes for chronic LBP.
phase_education.3:
**Phase 3: Functional Integration (Weeks 9–12)**

You are ready for demanding, everyday-relevant movements.

**Goal of this phase:** Transfer into real-life situations.

**Your strategy:**
- Complex movements: deadlifts, carries, single-leg exercises
- Transfer training to daily life and sport
- Maintain balance: increase intensity while keeping technique
- Long-term goal: sustainable, active lifestyle

**Scientific basis:** O'Sullivan et al. (2018): Functional restoration programs with structured exercise reduce disability long-term.

exercises.name: Cat-Camel
exercises.description: Quadruped position. Alternate between rounding the back (cat) and arching (camel). Move slowly and with control.

cognitive_cues.FAR: Your back is resilient and needs movement. This gentle mobilization is safe and causes no harm. Explore the full range of motion.
cognitive_cues.DER: Move slowly and mindfully. At the first signs of fatigue or strain, taking a break is perfectly fine — that's not a sign of weakness.
cognitive_cues.EER: Use your natural motivation productively. Focus on movement quality, not intensity or speed.
cognitive_cues.AR: Perform the movement with control. Focus on a smooth transition between positions.

exercises.phase_goal: Activate core stability and regain pain-free movement

exercises.name: Pelvic Tilt
exercises.description: Supine, knees bent. Gently tilt the pelvis forward and backward. Back stays relaxed on the floor.

cognitive_cues.FAR: This exercise shows you that you have control over your spine. Movement = healing. Pain up to 5/10 is normal and safe.
cognitive_cues.DER: Pay close attention to muscle activity. Stop when you feel tension. Less is more — quality over quantity.
cognitive_cues.EER: Your energy is valuable. Use it purposefully: every repetition with full attention, not mechanically.
cognitive_cues.AR: Focus on the neutral position of your pelvis. Small, controlled movements.

exercises.phase_goal: Activate core stability and regain pain-free movement

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.description: Supine, arms up, knees at 90°. Extend the opposite leg and reach the arm overhead. Alternate sides.

cognitive_cues.FAR: This exercise challenges your back — that's a good thing! Every repetition builds confidence that your back is stable.
cognitive_cues.DER: If one side is harder, do fewer reps on that side. Asymmetry is okay — your body is showing what it needs.
cognitive_cues.EER: Perfection is not the goal. Focus on clean technique rather than maximum reps. Better 6 good ones than 10 sloppy ones.
cognitive_cues.AR: Maintain core tension throughout the movement. Keep breathing steadily.

exercises.phase_goal: Activate core stability and regain pain-free movement

exercises.name: Hip Hinge (Romanian Deadlift)
exercises.description: Standing, light dumbbells. Push hips back, lean upper body forward. Keep the back straight.

cognitive_cues.FAR: This movement is one of the safest for your back — it trains exactly the movement pattern you need in daily life. Don't be afraid to increase the weight.
cognitive_cues.DER: Only increase weight when your technique is solid AND you feel good. Don't push on bad days — that's intelligence, not weakness.
cognitive_cues.EER: Progression doesn't just mean more weight. Better form is also progress. Celebrate technical improvements equally.
cognitive_cues.AR: Keep the back neutral. Movement comes from the hips, not the lower back.

exercises.phase_goal: Build resilience and strengthen back muscles

exercises.name: Plank (Forearm Support)
exercises.description: Support on forearms and toes. Body forms a straight line. Actively engage abs and glutes.

cognitive_cues.FAR: Tension in your back is a sign of activity, not damage. You are building strength. Hold on, even when it gets uncomfortable.
cognitive_cues.DER: If you start shaking: stop! That's your body saying "enough." Better 20s with good form than 40s with compensation.
cognitive_cues.EER: Timing matters: use a timer. Don't tack on "5 more seconds" — stick to the plan.
cognitive_cues.AR: Control your breathing. Don't hold your breath — keep breathing steadily.

exercises.phase_goal: Build resilience and strengthen back muscles

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.description: Standing, hold weight at chest level (kettlebell or dumbbell). Slowly lower into a squat and stand up with control.

cognitive_cues.FAR: Squats are excellent for your back — they train the entire system. Depth is safe as long as form is good. Go deeper than you think.
cognitive_cues.DER: Only go as deep as pain-free. On some days that will be less — accept that. Adaptation is strength.
cognitive_cues.EER: Focus on the 3-0-3 tempo. That's your speed limiter — it prevents enthusiasm from leading to injury.
cognitive_cues.AR: Chest up, weight on your heels. Knees track over your toes.

exercises.phase_goal: Build resilience and strengthen back muscles

exercises.name: Bird Dog
exercises.description: Quadruped position. Simultaneously extend the opposite arm and leg, hold 2 sec, then switch.

cognitive_cues.FAR: This anti-rotation exercise shows that your back can stay stable even under load. That's functional strength.
cognitive_cues.DER: Balance is difficult? Then reduce the range of motion. Shorter movements with control > long movements with wobbling.
cognitive_cues.EER: Count your reps deliberately. Don't go on autopilot — every repetition deserves attention.
cognitive_cues.AR: Hips and shoulders stay parallel to the floor. No trunk rotation.

exercises.phase_goal: Build resilience and strengthen back muscles

exercises.name: Deadlift
exercises.description: Standing, barbell or heavy dumbbells. Controlled lift with a straight back, hinging from the hips.

cognitive_cues.FAR: The deadlift is the king exercise for a robust back. Weight on the bar = proof that your back is strong. Increase boldly.
cognitive_cues.DER: Form over weight. Always. When technique suffers: reduce weight. Ego has no place here — your health does.
cognitive_cues.EER: Log your weight. Progression must be planned: max. 2.5 kg per week. Faster = risk.
cognitive_cues.AR: Diaphragmatic breathing, brace core before lifting. Bar stays close to the body.

exercises.name: Farmer's Carry
exercises.description: Heavy dumbbells in each hand, walk upright (20–30 m). Keep trunk stable, don't lean to the side.

cognitive_cues.FAR: This exercise simulates everyday loading — carrying groceries, luggage. It prepares you for real life. That's functional strength.
cognitive_cues.DER: Distance matters less than symmetric loading. Better 15 m with good form than 30 m with a crooked trunk.
cognitive_cues.EER: Use this exercise as a test, not a competition. If you lose form after 20 m: stop. No "just a bit more."
cognitive_cues.AR: Shoulders back, eyes forward. Even steps.

exercises.name: Split Squat (Bulgarian Split Squat)
exercises.description: Lunge position, rear foot elevated on a bench. Slowly lower down and push up.

cognitive_cues.FAR: Single-leg exercises are advanced — you're ready! Balance challenge = neurological training. Your back benefits.
cognitive_cues.DER: One side weaker? Start with the weak side, do fewer reps there. Balance out asymmetry, don't force it.
cognitive_cues.EER: Only add weight when you've completed 3 sessions in a row with 3x10 clean. Clear rule = protection from overenthusiasm.
cognitive_cues.AR: Upper body upright, front knee over toes. Back knee toward the floor.
